synoptic.summary: A short-lived ridge is giving way to a broad, slow-moving trough that brings several rounds of rain and snow from Thursday morning through Saturday morning. Thursday: strong flow from 170°–190° aloft (22–28 kt at ~3,400 ft above the landings, 30+ kt higher) keeps a gusty gradient from 150°–190° at the surface. The forecast discussion expects gusts of 20–25 kt from late Thursday morning and showers building into the afternoon. Friday: steady rain, with snow levels near 5,000 ft. A trailing wave Friday evening brings colder air, flow aloft turns to ~300° and snow can reach the valley floors (1–4 in). Saturday: the gradient collapses (flow aloft 1–6 kt up to ~5,000 ft above the landings) and the snow showers taper during the morning. Thunder chances stay at 0–5% throughout. The usual evening switch to 320°–360° is overridden by the gradient on Thursday and Friday.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: A longer duration storm will come through the area in pieces from Thursday morning through Saturday morning with the highest snow totals across the northern mountains and valley snow possible Friday evening into Saturday morning. … Snow levels will start much lower with this system with snow levels generally between 6000-6500 feet.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure fell from 1022.6 mb (07:54 Wed) to 1017.9 mb (18:54 Wed) as the trough approaches. Expect conditions to deteriorate through Friday and gusty flow from ~300° behind the Friday-evening wave.

observations.summary: Wednesday evening readings (18:15–18:49 local, about 12 h before the first slot) show the trough's gradient already in charge: flow from 143°–190° at 6–13 kt, gusting 15–23 kt, across the south valley and Utah Valley. Provo is calm. There is no evening switch to 320°–360°, which means the gradient has overridden the diurnal pattern. Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no data.
